extracted.intended_audience: users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (mathematicians / computational algebraists) who need to run and understand library procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation for SINGULAR library procedures (numerical decomposition, orbit parametrization, plane curve parametrization, binomial resolution, etc.) specifying usage, assumptions, returns, theory and examples. Intended to tell a practitioner what inputs are required, what each procedure computes, and known failure modes or constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: WitSet (witness point set decomposition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return: lists W(0..d) of witness point sets of i-dimensional components of V(J) for i=0,...,d respectively, where d the dimension of V(J), L list of generic linear polynomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: if W(i)=x, then V(J) has no component of dimension i. The procedure returns witness point sets for each pure-dimensional component of the variety V(J). Example usage shown with LIB "numerDecom.lib" and WitSet(I) returning W(1), W(0), and L (list of generic linear polynomials).

rubrics_metrics.name: NumIrrDecom (numerical irreducible decomposition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return: w(1),..., w(t) lists of irreducible witness point sets of irreducible components of V(J).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure from numerDecom.lib. Example demonstrates that the output encodes component dimensions and number of components; returned lists group irreducible components by their dimension. Users should interpret entries as corresponding irreducible witness point sets (0-, 1-, 2- dimensional, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: defl / deflation (deﬂation ideal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: defl(ideal I, int d); I ideal, int d order of the deﬂation. Return: deﬂation ideal DI of I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure in numerDecom.lib to compute the deflation ideal of order d. Example shows calling defl(I,1) and accessing the returned ideal DI. No extra assumptions are listed in this excerpt, but the parameter d specifies deflation order.

rubrics_metrics.name: NumPrimDecom (numerical primary decomposition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: NumPrimDecom(ideal I,int d); I ideal, d order of the deﬂation. Return: lists of the numerical primary decomposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure in numerDecom.lib. Example shows NumPrimDecom(I,1) returning witness point sets corresponding to numerical primary components. The order of deflation d controls the deflation step used during computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: orbitparam library: global requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To compute exp of the Lie algebra elements corresponding to parameters we require that the characteristic of the base field is zero or larger than n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overview: the orbitparam library implements Chevalley–Rosenlicht theorem to parametrize orbits of unipotent actions. The library assumes input matrices are strictly upper triangular and that the Lie span is closed under Lie bracket. If characteristic p > 0, dimensions n must be smaller than p in procedures that require nilpotency bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: tangentGens (tangent space generators and zeros)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: tangentGens(L,v); L list, v matrix. Return: list with four entries: (1) dimension of the orbit, (2) list of generators of the tangent space of the orbit of v at v (generators are elements of <L>), (3) list of matrices with coefficients to express generators as linear combinations of elements of L, (4) list of integers with entries in v which can be made zero by the action of exp(<L>).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume L is a list of strictly upper triangular n×n matrices of same size and the vector space <L> should be closed under Lie bracket. If the characteristic p of the ground field is positive, then n must be smaller than p. Theory: applies Chevalley–Rosenlicht. Example outputs illustrate the four-entry list structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: matrixExp (matrix exponential for nilpotent matrices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: matrixExp(A); A matrix. Assume: A is a nilpotent n×n matrix. If the characteristic p of the ground field is positive, then n has to be smaller than p. Return: matrix, exp(A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: compute the power series for exp(A), which terminates since A is nilpotent. Example shows explicit output for a small nilpotent matrix. The characteristic constraint prevents series truncation issues in positive characteristic.

rubrics_metrics.name: matrixLog (matrix logarithm for unipotent matrices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: matrixLog(A); A matrix. Assume: A−E is a nilpotent n×n matrix. If the characteristic p of the ground field is positive, then n has to be smaller than p. Return: matrix, log(A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: compute the power series for log(A) which terminates because A−E is nilpotent. Example demonstrates the output for a unipotent upper-triangular matrix.

rubrics_metrics.name: parametrizeOrbit (parametrization of orbit under exp(<L>))
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: parametrizeOrbit(L,v); L list, v matrix. Return: list with four entries: (1) int, dimension of the orbit, (2) matrix A over the basering giving a parametrization of the orbit of v under the action of exp(<L>), (3) list of integers (row-indices of entries which can be deleted by the action), (4) the variables of the parametrization to solve for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume L is a list of strictly upper triangular n×n matrices whose vector space <L> is closed under Lie bracket and v is an n×1 constant matrix. The basering must have at least size(L) variables, but only tangentGens(L,v)[1] many are used. Theory: compute tangent space generators, then apply matrixExp to generators, and take product to obtain parametrization. Examples show returned parametrization matrix entries and the variables used.

rubrics_metrics.name: maxZeros (find orbit element with many zeros)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: maxZeros(L,v); L list, v matrix. Return: matrix of constants over the basering giving an element in the orbit of v under exp(<L>) with (at least) as many zeros as the dimension of the orbit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume same constraints as parametrizeOrbit (strictly upper triangular matrices, <L> closed under Lie bracket, basering variable count, characteristic bounds). Theory: apply parametrizeOrbit and choose parameters from bottom to top to obtain an element with many zeros. Examples illustrate returned matrix with zeros in appropriate positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: paraplanecurves library: input and algorithm preconditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: rational parametrization of rational plane curves. Overview: suppose C = {f(x,y,z)=0} is a rational plane curve where f is homogeneous of degree n with coefficients in Q and absolutely irreducible (these conditions are checked automatically).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After preprocessing (projective automorphism via adjointIdeal), algorithm treats x transcendental and y algebraic, computes integral basis in C(x)[y] via normalization algorithms, obtains adjoint ideal by linear algebra or local singular analysis. For even degrees the final parametrization may require a quadratic field extension. The library depends on normalization/integral-basis routines and checks rationality (genus 0) automatically when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: adjointIdeal (compute adjoint ideal of a plane curve)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: adjointIdeal(f [, choices]); f polynomial in three variables. Return: ideal, the adjoint ideal of the curve defined by f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is a polynomial ring in three variables x,y,z with coefficients in Q. The polynomial f must be homogeneous and absolutely irreducible; these conditions will be checked automatically. Optional integer choices: 1 compute integral basis via normalization; 2 local analysis of singularities first (default); 3 normalization via ideal quotient; 4 normalization via local ideal quotient. Optional string choices include 'rattestyes' (cause error if curve not rational) and 'firstchecksdone' (prevent repeated checks). Theory and examples describe using integral bases and local analysis to obtain the adjoint ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: invertBirMap (invert a birational map)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: invertBirMap(phi, I); phi ideal, I ideal. Assume: phi represents a birational map of the variety given by ideal I to its image in projective space. Return: ring, the coordinate ring of the image with an ideal J defining the image and an ideal psi giving the inverse of phi (psi entries are representatives in R/J).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: the procedure might fail or give wrong output if phi does not define a birational map. Theory: compute ideal of the graph I(G) in R**S, intersect with S to get J, and obtain psi from linear relations in I(G) linear in the target variables. Example shows creation of ring with ideals J and psi and how to access them via setring.

rubrics_metrics.name: paraPlaneCurve (compute a rational parametrization for a rational plane curve)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: paraPlaneCurve(f [, s]); f polynomial, optional string s ('normal' or 'local'). Return: ring with an ideal PARA which contains a rational parametrization of the rational plane curve given by f; ground field is Q or a quadratic extension Q(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is polynomial ring in three variables with coefficients in Q; f must be homogeneous, absolutely irreducible, and the curve C must be rational (geometric genus 0); these conditions are checked automatically. Optional s: 'normal' compute integral basis via normalization, 'local' do local singularities first (default behaves like choice 2 in adjointIdeal). For even degree n, parametrization may be over a quadratic extension if no rational point exists on associated conic. Examples show PARA with three generators (homogeneous parametrization).

rubrics_metrics.name: rncAntiCanonicalMap (anticanonical map of a rational normal curve)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: rncAntiCanonicalMap(I); I homogeneous ideal in the basering defining a rational normal curve C in PP^n. Return: ideal defining the anticanonical map C -> PP^(n-2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: the procedure will fail or give wrong output if I is not the ideal of a rational normal curve. The entries of the returned ideal are representatives of elements in R/I. Theory: the anti-canonical map maps a rational normal curve isomorphically to a rational normal curve in PP^(n-2). Example shows mapping a computed RNC to anticanonical images.

rubrics_metrics.name: rationalPointConic (find rational point on conic or extend base field)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: rationalPointConic(p); p polynomial. Assume p is an irreducible quadratic polynomial in the first three ring variables; ground field expected to be Q. Return: ring R (either original basering if a rational point exists or a polynomial ring over a quadratic extension Q(a) if none exists) and defines a (1x3) matrix named 'point' containing coordinates of the point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method finds a point on the conic. Two cases: (1) rational point exists — R is unchanged; (2) no rational point — create quadratic extension Q(a) and produce point coordinates in that extension. The procedure returns the (possibly extended) ring. Example demonstrates both outcomes and shows minpoly for extension. Use testPointConic to verify.

rubrics_metrics.name: mapToRatNormCurve (map plane curve to rational normal curve)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: mapToRatNormCurve(f, AI); f polynomial, AI ideal (adjoint ideal). Assume: f is homogeneous in three variables and absolutely irreducible, the plane curve C defined by f is rational, and AI is the adjoint ideal of C. Return: ring with an ideal RNC (ideal of a rational normal curve).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is used as part of the pipeline: compute adjointIdeal then mapToRatNormCurve to obtain RNC used for further projection/parametrization steps. Example shows RNC with many defining equations.

rubrics_metrics.name: rncItProjOdd (iterate projection for odd degree rational normal curve)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: rncItProjOdd(I); I homogeneous ideal defining a rational normal curve C in PP^n with n odd. Return: ideal PHI defining an isomorphic projection of C to PP^1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: will fail or give wrong output if I is not ideal of a rational normal curve; the procedure tests whether n is odd. The entries of PHI are representatives in R/I. Theory: iterate anticanonical map to obtain PHI. Example shows computed PHI entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: rncItProjEven (iterate projection for even degree rational normal curve)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: rncItProjEven(I); I homogeneous ideal defining a rational normal curve C in PP^n with n even. Return: ring with an ideal CONIC defining a conic C2 in PP^2 and an ideal PHI defining an isomorphic projection of C to C2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: will fail or give wrong output if I is not the ideal of a rational normal curve; the procedure tests parity of n. The entries of PHI should be considered as representatives in R/I. For even n the projection target is a conic and a subsequent parametrization may require a rational point or quadratic extension (use rationalPointConic and paraConic). Examples demonstrate extraction of CONIC and PHI and subsequent use with paraConic.

rubrics_metrics.name: paraConic (parametrize a conic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: paraConic(q); q polynomial. Assume: basering is polynomial ring in three variables with coefficients in Q; q must be homogeneous degree 2 and absolutely irreducible. Return: ring with an ideal PARACONIC. The ring is the homogeneous coordinate ring of PP^1 and the ideal defines a rational parametrization PP^1 -> C2 = {q=0}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The method may fail if assumptions do not hold. Theory: compute a point on C2 via rationalPointConic, then invert the pencil of lines through that point to obtain the parametrization. Example shows PARACONIC = [s^2, s t, t^2] for a simple conic.

rubrics_metrics.name: testParametrization (verify parametrization equals curve)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: testParametrization(f, rTT); f polynomial, rTT ring. Return: int which is 1 if PARA in rTT defines a parametrization of the curve {f=0} and 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumptions: rTT has two variables and contains an ideal PARA as produced by paraPlaneCurve. Theory: compute the polynomial defining the image of PARA and compare it with f. Example returns 1 for a correct parametrization.

rubrics_metrics.name: testPointConic (verify a point lies on a conic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: testPointConic(p, r); p polynomial, r ring. Assume p is a homogeneous quadratic polynomial in the first three ring variables and r contains a (1x3) matrix named 'point' with entries from the ground field of r. Return: 1 iff the point lies on the conic given by p; 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This method temporarily changes the basering to r and restores it afterwards. Use this to validate the 'point' produced by rationalPointConic. Example shows testPointConic used in conditional to print 'point lies on conic'.

rubrics_metrics.name: BINresol (binomial resolution of singularities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: BINresol(J); J ideal. Return: E-resolution of singularities of a binomial ideal J in terms of the affine charts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure from resbinomial.lib implementing a combinatorial algorithm for resolution of binomial singularities (Blanco algorithm). Notes/Todos in library header warn about formatting, exports, and some poorly named internal procedures (identifyvars, elimrep, etc.). Example shows BINresol(J) returning a list of final charts with rings/ordering information; users should inspect returned chart list to interpret the resolution.
